column1: # MODE: PROD
# Which artifacts belong to which integration mode.
# A skill that offers more than one way to be driven declares it here, and
# `install.sh --integration <skill>=<mode>` picks one without a prompt, so an
# agent can choose its own interface headlessly.
# The rule is deliberately narrow: a binary named below installs ONLY in its
# mode, and every file not named installs in every mode. So SKILL.md and the
# binaries registry are never mode-dependent.
# `tailpipe-client-rs` is deliberately UNLISTED, not `skill`-only -- it is
# the reader AND the ingest path (piping stdin into a stream is inherently a
# shell operation, not something an MCP tool call can do), so it ships
# regardless of mode. Naming it directly in a `skill` row here (as an
# earlier version of this file did) made the installer's generic
# bin/-gating logic (file_allowed in src/installer/src/integration.rs)
# treat it as skill-mode-EXCLUSIVE instead, silently dropping it from every
# mcp-mode install -- confirmed for real installing the published
# v2.0.0-alpha.6 release. `skill`'s row below names `-`, a placeholder
# file_allowed/binary_mode can never match a real file, purely so `skill`
# still appears in modes() and `--integration tailpipe=skill` validates and
# means something concrete -- the same precedent decisions/integration.tsv
# already set for its own always-on CLI binary. `mcp` additionally installs
# tailpipe-mcp -- the consumer an agent calls as typed tools instead of
# shelling out for every read/search/wait/save.
# tailpipe-server-rs is likewise deliberately UNLISTED, not skill-only.
# Somebody has to run the server, and in mcp mode that somebody is the same
# agent: the adapter finds a server (via TAILPIPE_ENDPOINT or its own
# default path) and does not start one.
mode
skill
column3: No binary of its own beyond tailpipe-client-rs (unlisted/always-on); this row exists only so `skill` validates as a real --integration choice

column1: mcp
column3: MCP consumer an agent calls as typed tools instead
